title: Extracellular ATP signaling regulates systemic calcium signaling in the response of Arabidopsis seedlings to local wounding
content:
Abstract
The response of plants to local environmental stimuli can be activated in the tissues or organs that are directly challenged or systemically in remote and unstressed tissues or organs. Extracellular ATP (eATP) is known to play key roles in regulating many physiological processes in plants. Here, we demonstrated that local wounding at a leaf or root of Arabidopsis seedling triggers a transient systemic increase in eATP levels, preceding the systemic elevation of cytosolic free calcium concentration ([Ca2+]cyt) in remote, un-wounded tissues. By using GCaMP3-p2k1 single-mutant, GCaMP3-p2k2 single-mutant, and GCaMP3-p2k1p2k2 double-mutant plants, it was found that local wounding-induced increases of [Ca2+]cyt at systemic tissues were weakened by mutation of P2Ks (eATP receptors). These results indicate that eATP/P2Ks are involved in regulating local and systemic enhancement of [Ca2+]cyt in response to local wounding.
